newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds weaken on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds weaken on profit-taking.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker in steady trading on Thursday as investors continued to take profits ahead of Canadian employment and U.S. producer prices due to be released on Friday, analysts said.
"The market is heavy. We saw sellers overnight and we're seeing a bit more selling from the corporates this morning," said a trader at a Canadian-based brokerage.
"There's just a little bit of profit-taking occurring in the market right now ahead of tomorrow's producer prices in the U.S.," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with New York-based I.D.E.A.
Canada's benchmark 30-year long bond fell C$0.22 to C$118.27 to yield 6.592 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond lost 5/32 to yield 6.58 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds moved to a spread of one basis point, the same as at the close on Wednesday.

Analysts said the weaker performance of U.S. treasuries and a soft Canadian dollar spilled over into the Canadian bond market. Canada's dollar opened firmer on Thursday at C$1.3725 (US$0.7286) amid German hedge fund buying of the unit in overnight trade.
But the currency weakened off of its overnight highs as some North American traders sold the unit ahead of this morning's major economic data.

"The (Canada) dollar is a little bit off, so there's a bit more weight on the bonds," said Kalirai, who added that the markets were awaiting the release of Friday's employment data in Canada and producer prices in the United States.

A Reuters survey of economists predicted a jump of 38,800 jobs in employment growth for June, compared to an increase of 61,000 in May. Canadian unemployment is expected to dip to 9.4 percent in June from 9.5 percent in May.
A Reuters U.S. survey forecast producer prices would remain unchanged in June from a drop of 0.3 percent in May.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.15 to C$109.27 to yield 5.991 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent, which lost 3/32 to yield 6.27 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 28 basis points from 29 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.09 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.13 percent.
